Echo State Networks (ESNs) are a type of recurrent neural network used for processing time-series data. They consist of a large, fixed-size, randomly connected hidden layer called the "reservoir," which processes the input data. The weights of the reservoir are typically fixed and not trained directly. Instead, only the output weights are adjusted to fit the desired output. Training in ESNs usually involves adjusting the output weights to minimize the error between the network's output and the target output.
